_meta.note: SAMPLE RULES DATA for the BGN Documentation Reference — modern hobby board games. Concise table references to publicly documented rules; always defer to your physical rulebook for the authoritative text. This file demonstrates the 'groups = games' pattern for modern board games.

entries.name: Wingspan Setup
entries.subtitle: Build your bird sanctuary

blocks.t: Each player takes a **player mat** (with three habitat rows: Forest, Grassland, Wetland), 5 action cubes, 8 food tokens, and a hand of **8 bird cards** (keep 5). Shuffle the bird deck and deal the bird tray, and lay out the goal board, bonus cards, and round scoring cards.
Each round has a **goal** (e.g. birds in a habitat, eggs laid, birds with a trait) scored at round end. Draw 3 bonus cards and keep 1-2 — they score at the end of the game.

entries.text: wingspan setup build your bird sanctuary player mat habitat food bird cards

entries.name: Turn Structure
entries.subtitle: Four rounds, four actions

blocks.t: The game lasts **4 rounds**. On your turn, place one of your 8 action cubes onto one of the **4 actions**: gain food (Forest), lay eggs (Grassland), draw birds (Wetland), or **play a bird** from your hand into an empty slot (the habitat it enters determines its on-turn effect).

items: **Gain food** — take a food die (reroll tokens when the feeder is empty); get more if birds in the Forest row have 'gain food' powers.
**Lay eggs** — place eggs on birds in the Grassland row (one per bird); each egg is worth 1 point at the end.
**Draw birds** — draw 2 cards into your hand (one to your tray).
**Play a bird** — pay its food cost and egg cost, then resolve its brown, pink, or white power.

blocks.t: When all players have placed their cubes the round ends: score the round goal, return all cubes, and start the next round. Round 1 has 8 turns per player, shrinking by 2 each round.

entries.text: turn structure wingspan four rounds four actions gain food lay eggs draw birds play a bird

entries.name: Scoring
entries.subtitle: Points from every direction

items: **Points on bird cards** — each bird's printed point value.
**Food in your supply** — 1 point per 5 food.
**Bonus cards** — points per their condition (e.g. tucked birds, habitat diversity, predator birds).

blocks.t: Most points after the 4 rounds wins. Ties break in favor of the player with the most eggs.

entries.text: scoring wingspan points from every direction bird cards eggs food bonus cards tucked

entries.name: Azul Setup
entries.subtitle: Decorate the palace of Évora

blocks.t: Each player takes a **player board** (5 pattern rows, a wall, and a floor line). Place 4 **factory displays** in a circle around the middle, and place 100 tiles of 5 colors in the bag. The first player takes the **starting player** token.
Each round, tiles are drawn from the bag and placed 4 at a time on each factory display until the bag is empty.

entries.text: azul setup decorate the palace of évora player board factory displays tiles

entries.name: Drafting & Placing Tiles
entries.subtitle: Clean pattern lines, complete walls

blocks.t: On your turn take **all the tiles of one color** from a factory display (or from the middle) and place them on one of your **pattern rows** — each row holds a set number of tiles (row 1 = 1 tile, row 5 = 5). A color can't be in a row that already contains another color, or already be placed in that row's wall position.

When a row is **complete**, move one tile to the matching square on your wall (row + column must be empty there) and score it. **Leftover tiles** go to your **floor line**, which deducts points at round end. If the middle is empty when you take tiles, you take the starting player token.

Wall scoring: 1 point for the tile + 1 for each adjacent tile horizontally and vertically (chains add up to big scores). Complete a **row or column** and you get a +2 bonus; complete all 5 of a color, +7.

entries.text: drafting and placing tiles azul clean pattern lines complete walls floor line scoring

entries.name: End of Round & Game
entries.subtitle: Refill and play again

blocks.t: When all tiles have been drafted, score the round: wall tiles score now (already counted at placement), floor line tiles **subtract** 1/2/3/4/6/8/11 points in order. Discard floor tiles, fill the factories with fresh tiles, and the player holding the starting token begins the next round.
The game ends when a player **completes a horizontal row** of their wall. Play finishes the round, then the player with the **most points** wins.

entries.text: end of round and game azul refill and play again most points wins

entries.name: Ticket to Ride Setup
entries.subtitle: Claim railways across the map

blocks.t: Shuffle the train cards (locomotives are wildcards) and deal **4 train cards** to each player, plus **3 destination tickets** (keep at least 2 — discard the rest). Give each player 45 colored train pieces (for the USA map).
Players choose starting colors. Turn order proceeds clockwise.

entries.text: ticket to ride setup claim railways across the map train cards destination tickets 45 trains

entries.name: Turn Structure
entries.subtitle: Draw, claim, or ticket

blocks.t: On your turn take **one** of three actions: **draw train cards** (2 face-up cards, or 1 face-down from the deck, or 1 face-up locomotive as your whole turn), **claim a route** (play matching colored cards to place trains on a route between two cities), or **draw destination tickets** (draw 3, keep at least 1).

To claim a route, play the number of train cards matching its length and color (gray routes accept any single color). Long routes earn more points but require many cards. A player may only use each route once, and once claimed it's blocked for others.

entries.text: turn structure ticket to ride draw claim or ticket draw train cards claim a route draw destination tickets

entries.name: Scoring & End of Game
entries.subtitle: Longest route bonus

blocks.t: Routes score their printed value when claimed (1–15 points by length). The game ends when a player has **2 or fewer trains left**, and everyone gets one final turn.

Final scoring: add all completed route points + each **completed destination ticket**'s value. **Uncompleted tickets subtract** their value. The player with the **longest continuous route** gets a +10 bonus. Highest total wins.

entries.text: scoring and end of game ticket to ride longest route bonus destination tickets subtract

entries.name: Cascadia Setup
entries.subtitle: Build a balanced wilderness

blocks.t: Each player takes a **starting habitat** tile (with a naturalist token on it). Shuffle the habitat tiles and wildlife tokens, and reveal a market of **4 habitat tiles + 4 wildlife tokens**. Choose a scoring variant for the 5 animal types (or draft scoring cards).
Each animal type (Elk, Bear, Salmon, Hawk, Fox) has a scoring pattern — e.g. elk score in pairs, bears score in pairs of adjacent groups, salmon score in runs.

entries.text: cascadia setup build a balanced wilderness habitat tiles wildlife tokens elk bear salmon hawk fox

entries.name: Turn Structure
entries.subtitle: Pick a tile, place a token

blocks.t: On your turn, choose **one habitat tile** from the market along with one wildlife token (matching or not), place the tile adjacent to your wilderness (its terrain must be compatible), then place the token on the tile.

When a habitat or wildlife is taken, reveal a replacement. If a market slot becomes empty you may reveal a new card; if the market fills with a **naturalist token**, the player with the most tokens gains a bonus 2 points at the end.

entries.text: turn structure cascadia pick a tile place a token habitat wildlife naturalist

entries.name: Scoring
entries.subtitle: Habitats and wildlife

blocks.t: At the end of the game (when the habitat deck runs out and all players have taken their final turn), score in two parts: **habitats** (each connected region of the same terrain scores area points based on size — a group of 4-5 tiles is worth more than two pairs) and **wildlife** (each animal type scores its chosen variant, e.g. pairs of adjacent elk, largest contiguous bear herds, salmon in longest runs).
Add the naturalist bonus (+2 for the most naturalist tokens). The highest total wins.

entries.text: scoring cascadia habitats and wildlife habitat regions wildlife tokens naturalist bonus

entries.name: Everdell Setup
entries.subtitle: Build a city of critters

blocks.t: Each player takes a **critter village board**, a hand of 8 cards (keep 6), and starts the first **season** (Spring). Shuffle the meadow deck and lay out 8 meadow cards; place the event cards and the seasonal action spaces in order.
Each season unlocks a new set of **action spaces** (place workers there): Spring grants 2 workers, Summer 2 more, Autumn 2 more, and Winter has no new workers but grants special end-game actions.

entries.text: everdell setup build a city of critters critter village board meadow cards seasons workers

entries.name: Turns & Seasons
entries.subtitle: Workers, cards, and seasons

blocks.t: On your turn, either **place a worker** on an available action space or **play a card** from your hand (pay its cost: resources and/or previous cards in a chain). Play continues around the table until everyone has used all their workers.

items: **Play a card** — build a critter or construction into your city (up to 15 cards). Cards give resources, points, and ongoing effects.
**Workers** — Place on: basic resources, a card's production spaces, the meadow draw, or the event.
**Prepare for the next season** — when you're done, flip your board to the next season, gain its new workers, and score your season-specific event.

entries.text: turns and seasons everdell workers cards and seasons play a card place a worker prepare for the next season

entries.name: Scoring
entries.subtitle: Points for the city

blocks.t: The game ends after the Winter season when no players have cards or actions left. **Score**: each card's printed points + event points + points from city cards like the Castle, plus the end-game scoring for cards with ongoing effects (e.g. points per occupied action, points per forest card).
The player with the **most points** wins. Ties go to the player with the most resources remaining.
